rationale: The literature does not substantiate the claim that autism spectrum features, ADHD/hyperactivity, and sleep disturbances are present in 50-75% of assessed individuals with Popov-Chang syndrome (YWHAZ-related neurodevelopmental disorder). In the primary cohort defining the condition (Popov et al., 2019), only 1 of 5 (20%) assessed individuals presented with autism, directly contradicting the 50-75% range. Furthermore, specific cohort-level quantifications demonstrating sleep disturbances or ADHD at 50-75% prevalence across YWHAZ cohorts are absent from the literature.

evidence.text: Popov et al. (2019) identified YWHAZ variants in five individuals with neurodevelopmental phenotypes, but only one individual (20%) was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic phenotypic frequency of behavioral abnormalities, sleep disturbances, and ADHD across an expanded worldwide cohort of individuals with pathogenic de novo YWHAZ variants?
new_directions.rationale: Popov-Chang syndrome has only been characterized in very small series (e.g., n=5 in the index report); gathering a larger international registry cohort is required to establish accurate phenotypic penetrance and frequencies.
